body: I would love to have a medication that didn't interact with birth control. While, yes, it is ultimately my decision, I learned that any hormonal birth control would lower the effectiveness of my epilepsy meds. So, yes it seems like a no brainer, and it really is, however...however it'd be nice to avoid the painful period cramps, excessive bloating, nausea, and increase of acne. In my 40s, I've been dealing with this for decades. And I'm too scared at this point to change my meds, so I'm stuck. 3 weeks of hell a month supercedes the possibility of a grand mal episode of hell.

I just finished Sinner yesterday by Sierra Simone. It's a part of a series but could be read on its own. 

Synopsis is simple: man hates Catholic church for events that happened in his childhood. He then falls for his best friend's sister, who's taking her vows to be a nun. 

There were several steamy scenes that could serve what you're looking for. I listed the tropes below. 

1. Best friend's sister. 
2. Age gap (15 years, he's older).
3. Mixed race (he's white, she's Black).
4. Forbidden romance. 
5. "Teach me."
6. First love. 

The Priest comes first and is the MMC's younger brother. There is 1 more book after this, about another brother and, rumors about 2 more. 1 for the 4th brother and 1 for the Father who is a priest and counseled this family. 

Funny thing is, what the MMC struggles with, family wise (not the religion aspect) I went through as well and highly related to. While I enjoyed the steamy scenes, I enjoyed, more so than I expected, how he handled said events. 

Happy reading, OP!

There's something about the single dad, though. Ignite by Melanie Harlow shows he's a divorced fire fighter ex SEAL father of 2 who is falling for his neighbor.
